findings.conclusion: Nested controller exclusively owns target stdin. Its termination is real. Target seals startup input after accepting finite work, independently joins native threads and tears down. Relay ignores controller EOF after start. Observer remains alive and holds identity/wait handles, not target control input.

New ACK service alone owns bridge binding. OS supplies connecting PID; process creation time and live retained handle constrain replacement. Target identity, epoch and fixture lease checked before swap. Live detached old bridge is rejected; dead old bridge can be replaced without reopening target stdin. The command-line lease is not authentication against malicious same-user processes.

Observed highwater is a separate durable transaction; accept commits before receipt, receipt before ACK. Real receiver death before/after COMMIT recovers and deduplicates. Early-ACK controls actually release seq1 with zero database rows and fail correct assertions.

OS target binding is re-probed before ledger reconciliation, which independently rechecks it inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Termination is not inferred from ACK I/O failure. Final durable sessions clear active atomically; repeated terminal restart returns identical detail. Every final proof is same_process_signaled. Unknown tail stays true.

Real SQLite writer contention persists through target exit. Long contention produces explicit deadline/deferred; SQLITE_FULL comes from a real page-count cap and attempted padding insertion inside the accept transaction. Both leave active state until a later receiver reconciles. Closing a killed receiver stdin can raise due to a buffered failed resume write; now tolerated only after observing child exit, without rewriting exit code.

Initial normal/receiver-after attempts failed due to fixture quit protocol and killed stdin cleanup; preserved verbatim. Final matrix and final negative controls use archived sources and the same native executable. Independent audit copies database, WAL and SHM before read-only inspection and compares original hashes. Every spawned process has an actual exit code.

This is a bounded, paced cooperative fixture. No strict throughput/deadline bound, arbitrary lifetime, hostile IPC, external database deletion/rename race or exhaustive startup/bridge reconnect race coverage. Receiver restarts are bounded, not a production supervision policy. No trusted producer final watermark, so copied-but-uncommitted records are protocol-discarded on terminal close. OS death and SQLite COMMIT are not atomic.

Next use a NEW owned fixture to exercise real shared-slot WRITE access violations and torn-publication exclusion. Current protected-page failures are reads at known copy sites; do not broaden to arbitrary exception suppression.
